At a glance

Use the client’s view to make safer network decisions.

Wi-Fins-3MABGNNSafe RL
System problem

Enterprise Wi-Fi changes on several timescales. Short interference bursts need fast, local reactions; channel assignments and power policies need slower, network-wide planning. Decisions must also respect service-level objectives for voice, exams, guests, streaming, and IoT traffic.

Architecture

The design expands the access point’s view with client measurements, transport quality, and fine-time measurement. A fast loop detects airtime or interference spikes and applies bounded mitigation. A slow loop builds an interference graph, ranks channels with bandit feedback, and evaluates network-wide configurations.

Safety layer & evidence

A graph neural network predicts throughput, latency, and retry behaviour for candidate states. Policies are checked against per-service constraints before deployment; unsafe actions are rejected or rolled back. Reported GNN error was 7.4 percent on seen and 8.04 percent on unseen configurations.

Contribution & collaboration

Medha contributed to the adaptive decision pipeline, power estimation, simulation, system integration, and final presentation as part of IIT Madras Team 46 for the Arista Networks challenge at IIT Patna.
